subject: minibatches and data subsampling for ADVI?

messages.author: 04c3b84e29590e2b
messages.subject: minibatches and data subsampling for ADVI?
parts:
I have been using stan's ADVI implementation for NMF with some success (thanks guys!) and would like to try out data subsampling for the stochastic gradient ascent on larger matrices. So far I haven't found any API parameters that seem to support this, although it is claimed as a feature in the NIPS paper on ADVI. After digging around a bit I was able to find this recipe:
https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/adsvi/how_to_ADSVI.md

Is that the recommended approach, and if so, are there plans to integrate the changes on that branch with master?

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] minibatches and data subsampling for ADVI?
parts:
The NIPS paper was custom code on the C++ side---it's not part
of Stan's API yet.

- Bob

that branch of stan will work. (do note that it uses an older stan version (v2.9.0).) as it describes, you will have to hard-code how data subsampling is performed in the generated `.hpp` file.

best,
dustin

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] minibatches and data subsampling for ADVI?
parts:
I don't think anyone's actively working on data streaming
for ADVI for Stan. I'd suggest looking at Alp and Dustin's
package Edward:

http://edwardlib.org

Its home page says it supports stochastic variational inference.

- Bob
